changelog: Fibonacci retracement rebuilt against the TradingView reference screenshots supplied with this ticket. Verified in the same Playwright + Chrome for Testing harness as v3.21.1 (real js/chart.js + js/backtest.js + js/backtest-drawings.js, mocked backend) -- every item below was reproduced before the fix and confirmed after it.

1. Labels jammed against the price axis -- v3.21.1's own fix anchored fib labels at the overlay CANVAS's right edge, which is wider than the chart's actual plot area: Lightweight Charts reserves real pixel width (confirmed via its own tvChart.priceScale('right').width() API, 64px in the reference layout) for the right price scale, and the label was drawn past the plot area into that reserved strip, overlapping the axis and, at extend-right, every other level's label at the same x. Fixed: labels are now clamped to (canvas width − live price-scale width), and always anchored at their own line's actual right end rather than the canvas edge. Verified in-browser: every label renders inside the plot area, at a distinct on-screen position per level, never past the price scale.

2. Drawn edge-to-edge instead of between anchors -- extend_right defaulted true, stretching every level line across the whole canvas regardless of where the two anchors were placed. Replaced with an explicit extend setting ('none' / 'right' / 'both'), defaulting to 'none' -- a fresh fib now draws only between its own two anchors, exactly where drawn, matching the reference. Extend right/both are still available and confirmed to still clamp their own labels to the plot area rather than the extended line's own edge.

3. Settings dialog rebuilt to match the TradingView reference: trend line on/off with its own colour and style (the diagonal connector between the two anchors, independent of the horizontal levels); levels line width and style; the Extend dropdown from item 2; Prices, Levels, Levels format (values/percent), label side (left/right), label position (top/middle/bottom), font size, background shading with its own opacity slider, and Reverse; the full per-level checkbox+colour list, now covering TradingView's standard ratio set (0, 0.236, 0.382, 0.5, 0.618, 0.65, 0.786, 1, 1.272, 1.414, 1.618, 2.618, 3.618, 4.236) with only 0/0.382/0.5/0.618/0.786/1 checked by default, exactly as specified. Every control applies live (both 'input' and 'change' are wired, so a colour or opacity slider updates the drawing while it's still being dragged, not just on release) and persists via the existing update_backtest_drawing endpoint. Verified in-browser: toggling a level, changing the Extend mode, and changing a level's colour all update the rendered drawing and are sent to the (mocked) backend immediately.

4a. Replay speed dropdown -- traced directly, not guessed at: the current source (pages/backtest.php) already defines all four options (1x/2x/5x/10x) and nothing in the codebase manipulates that element's options at runtime. Rendered the exact markup in a real browser at four viewport widths and confirmed all four options are present and the selected value displays correctly every time -- could not reproduce 'empty' from the current source. If this is still visible on a live/deployed environment, it points to a stale cached asset rather than a source defect (the same class of issue this project has hit before -- see CLAUDE.md v3.16.3); a hard refresh or a fresh Update Now should resolve it without a code change.

4b. Duplicate/stacked fib objects -- confirmed in-browser that a single draw gesture creates exactly one backtest_drawings row (one add_backtest_drawing call per gesture) and that deleting a drawing issues an unconditional, ownership-checked DELETE FROM backtest_drawings WHERE id=? server-side (includes/controllers/BacktestDrawingController.php::delete()) -- there is no soft-delete flag and nothing left behind. The most likely source of the stacking seen in the reference screenshot was the v3.21.0/v3.21.1-era dragging and magnet bugs (fixed in v3.21.1) prompting repeated near-identical retries, each one narrowly passing the old exact-point-match cancel guard and saving a new near-duplicate. Hardened defensively regardless: the accidental-click cancel guard now checks real on-screen pixel distance (under ~7px) instead of exact time/price equality, so a shaky retry on top of an existing drawing no longer saves a stacked duplicate.

Verified per the ticket's own checklist: drew a fib low-to-high, confirmed six labelled levels with readable ratio and price inside the plot area; dragged both anchors; opened settings and toggled levels, colours and extend live; then panned, zoomed, and simulated a timeframe switch/replay step (a full candle-array replacement, the same operation js/backtest.js performs on every step) -- the drawing's on-screen position recomputed correctly and it was never lost.
release_notes: No schema changes in this release -- nothing to migrate. Per instruction, nothing was deployed as part of this turn.
